blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Strategic sourcing and category management are the disciplines that turn procurement from a reactive, transaction-by-transaction activity into a proactive lever for competitive advantage. Categories are groups of similar purchases — packaging, energy, IT services, logistics — each managed by someone who becomes, over time, a serious expert in that specific market.

What separates strategic sourcing from ordinary buying is the time horizon. Strategic sourcing thinks in years, not weeks. It maps the supplier landscape, understands the cost drivers, anticipates the next cycle, and positions the company to benefit when the market moves. Reactive buying, by contrast, calls three suppliers when the current contract expires and chooses the cheapest quote.

The difference over a decade is enormous. A company with strong category management pays meaningfully less for the same inputs, absorbs shocks more calmly, and often knows about supplier problems before the suppliers themselves do. That is not buying — it is a quiet form of market intelligence that happens to live in the procurement function.

items.q: According to the text, what turns procurement into a lever for competitive advantage?
items.why: "Strategic sourcing and category management are the disciplines that turn procurement… into a proactive lever for competitive advantage."

items.q: What primarily distinguishes strategic sourcing from ordinary buying?
items.why: "What separates strategic sourcing from ordinary buying is the time horizon."

items.q: The final line calls category management "a quiet form of market intelligence." This most likely suggests that…
options: procurement should be run by the marketing team
market intelligence is unrelated to buying
the value of good sourcing goes well beyond negotiating price
items.why: Inferência: o autor eleva a função para além da compra — ela gera conhecimento de mercado, não só preço.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Strong sourcing helps a company absorb shocks.
Calling three suppliers at contract expiry is a sound long-term strategy.
items.why: Inferência: o texto retrata essa prática reativa como o oposto do sourcing estratégico que defende.

items.q: The claim that such a firm "often knows about supplier problems before the suppliers themselves do" implies that category managers…
options: spend most of their time auditing invoices
develop deep, forward-looking insight into their markets
items.why: Inferência: só um domínio profundo do mercado explica antecipar problemas — coerente com "maps the supplier landscape… anticipates the next cycle".

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver apresentando ao comitê o plano da nova função de gestão por categoria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. Before I walk you through the categories, let me be blunt about where we are today. For fifteen years, procurement here has been a string of one-off negotiations. Someone needs packaging, they ring a couple of suppliers the week the contract runs out, and they take the lowest number on the table. It feels efficient. It is, in fact, quite expensive.

What I am proposing is that we carve our spend into a handful of categories — logistics, raw materials, professional services, energy — and put a genuine owner behind each one. Not a buyer. An owner. Someone whose job, over three to five years, is to understand that market better than anyone else in the room.

Now, I want to manage expectations. In year one, the savings will look modest, and one or two of you will ask whether this was worth the headcount. Please resist that instinct. The real return shows up when the market turns and we are the only ones who saw it coming.

So I am not asking you to sign off on a number today. I am asking you to back a shift in mindset — from buying things to owning markets.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Oliver describe procurement over the past fifteen years?
items.why: "For fifteen years, procurement here has been a string of one-off negotiations."

items.q: What does Oliver want behind each category?
items.why: "put a genuine owner behind each one. Not a buyer. An owner."

items.q: Why does Oliver say "It feels efficient. It is, in fact, quite expensive"?
options: The lowest quote often ignores longer-term and total cost
The company buys in the wrong currency
The negotiations take too many hours
items.why: Inferência: escolher o menor número imediato aparenta economia, mas custa caro no horizonte longo — a tese do sourcing estratégico.

items.q: When Oliver says the return "shows up when the market turns and we are the only ones who saw it coming," he is implying that…
options: the value is mainly in avoiding all suppliers
savings are guaranteed in the first year
category expertise creates foresight that competitors lack
market timing is a matter of luck
items.why: Inferência: o ganho vem do conhecimento antecipado do mercado, que a concorrência não tem.

items.q: What is Oliver actually asking the committee to approve today?
options: A shift in mindset, from buying things to owning markets
items.why: "I am not asking you to sign off on a number today. I am asking you to back a shift in mindset."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our time horizon is three to five years, not the next quarter." A time horizon is…
options: the deadline for a single contract
the period over which decisions are planned and judged
the working hours of the team
items.why: Time horizon = horizonte temporal: o período sobre o qual se planeja e se avalia.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A category manager who cannot read the ___ cannot anticipate where prices are heading."
items.why: Supplier landscape = panorama de fornecedores, o que se lê para antecipar preços.

items.q: "Energy and freight are the two main cost drivers in this category." A cost driver is…
options: a factor that materially determines the cost
items.why: Cost driver = driver de custo: o fator que efetivamente determina o custo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A resilient sourcing function lets the company ___ shocks without passing every price rise to customers."
items.why: To absorb = absorver: encaixar o choque sem repassar imediatamente.

items.q: Market intelligence is best described as…
options: the credit rating of each supplier
the archive of past purchase orders
actionable insight into how a market behaves and where it is heading
items.why: Market intelligence = inteligência de mercado: conhecimento acionável sobre o comportamento e a direção do mercado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de procurement e sourcing. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the sourcing strategy." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out category management one spend area at a time." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the extra headcount." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the supplier plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Chasing one more cent per unit won't move the needle on total cost of ownership." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
